Despite being held captive, she is able to convert her Muslim captors to Christianity through her wisdom and piety. She is described as beautiful, passionate and proud, and her love for Orlando leads her to renounce her Muslim faith and embrace Christianity. This work is a reflection of the cultural and religious tensions that existed in Spain during the late 19th century, and the novel can be seen as an expression of the desire to assimilate Andalusian culture into the Spanish national identity.
